## Why human

The blog series IS the personal-brand catalyst (`docs/MARKET_POSITION_2026-06.md` §7, STRATEGIC_ROADMAP #14) — it must be the maintainer's voice and carry real engineering detail only the author has. AI may outline/edit; authorship is human.

## The four posts (each a distinct search-landing surface)

1. "Why I licensed my VS Code extension AGPL — knowing the cost" — the decision, the May counter-case, why adoption-tax was accepted; this post does the work of making the license a brand asset.
2. "Round-trip correctness in a ProseMirror markdown editor" — publish alongside ROUNDTRIP_REPORT (#003); the technical flag-plant.
3. "Webview trust: building a VS Code extension that earns enterprise allowlists" — pairs with SECURITY_POSTURE (#025); reference CVE-2025-65716 factually.
4. "Reading-first: the markdown UX nobody builds for" — pairs with the measure/UX release (#011-#016) and the new hero (#028).

## Sequencing

One per ~3 weeks starting at GA. Each ends with the same one-line install CTA. Cross-post (dev.to/HN where fit is organic; no growth-hacks).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Publication platform chosen (own domain preferred for SEO accrual)
- [ ] Posts 1–2 published within 6 weeks of GA; 3–4 scheduled
- [ ] Each post linked from README/docs where topical
